skill.name: datadata-dql
skill.description: Write Datadata DQL scripts for data querying, cleaning, transformation, DataFrame operations, HTTP integration, and simple visualization.
skill.summary: Create platform-specific Datadata DQL scripts with Starlark syntax, SQL queries, DataFrame logic, and validation steps.
skill.author: datadata-team

security_audit.summary: No evidence of prompt injection, malware, or install-time execution was found. The static findings are false positives from Markdown code formatting, type-stub docstrings, SQL examples, and documented DQL fetch examples that use placeholder domains. The skill does describe network-capable DQL scripts, so users should approve real endpoints and data sharing before running generated scripts.

content.value_statement: Writing Datadata DQL scripts requires platform-specific Starlark syntax and data APIs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create query, fetch, DataFrame, and validation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Datadata DQL scripts that return DataFrame, list, dict, or serializable results.
Uses documented query, fetch, DataFrame, Series, time, math, JSON, and canvas APIs.
Explains when to inspect raw data before writing final transformation logic.
Applies parameterized SQL examples to reduce injection risk in generated queries.
Builds examples for cleaning, aggregating, joining, validating, and exporting data.
limitations: It cannot verify live Datadata schemas unless table and column details are provided.
It does not execute DQL or inspect runtime results by itself.
External API calls require user-approved endpoints, credentials, and data sharing rules.
It focuses on Datadata DQL, not general Python compatibility.

use_cases.title: Prepare Analytics Scripts
use_cases.description: Create DQL scripts that query business tables, aggregate metrics, and return validated results for dashboards.

use_cases.title: Clean Operational Data
use_cases.description: Generate transformations that remove duplicates, fill missing values, and standardize fields before downstream use.

use_cases.title: Prototype Data Integrations
use_cases.description: Combine SQL query results with approved external API responses and return a structured dataset for review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Query Script
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple table inspection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Datadata DQL script that queries [table], limits results to [row count], and returns the DataFrame for inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Clean and Validate Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DQL script that reads [table], removes duplicate rows by [key], handles missing [field], and returns a small validation summary.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Aggregation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Datadata DQL to calculate [metric] by [dimension] for [date range], using SQL filtering first and DataFrame operations only when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate External API Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that combines internal and external data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe DQL workflow that queries [internal data], fetches approved data from [API endpoint], validates both structures, and returns merged results.

output_examples.input: Create a DQL script to compare current month revenue with previous month revenue.
output_examples.output: The result includes a script plan that queries both periods, calculates revenue change, handles zero previous revenue, and returns comparison fields.

output_examples.input: Clean a customer table before an RFM analysis.
output_examples.output: The result describes a DQL workflow that checks required columns, removes duplicates, validates missing values, and returns a prepared customer dataset.

output_examples.input: Inspect an external API response before transforming it.
output_examples.output: The result returns the response type and sample body first, so the user can confirm structure before final transformation logic is written.

best_practices: Read the relevant reference file before using a DQL API or object method.
Use parameterized query arguments instead of concatenating user input into SQL.
Return a small sample first when table schemas or API response structures are uncertain.
anti_patterns: Do not assume API response field order without inspecting actual returned data.
Do not return unbounded datasets when a LIMIT or aggregation would answer the request.
Do not use unsupported Python features such as imports, classes, try blocks, or file I/O.

faq.question: What is Datadata DQL?
faq.answer: DQL is a Datadata scripting language based on Starlark with built-in APIs for querying and processing data.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it run the generated script?
faq.answer: No. It helps write scripts, but runtime execution and result inspection happen in the Datadata environment.

faq.question: Does it support external HTTP requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the DQL fetch API, but users should approve endpoints, credentials, and shared data first.

faq.question: How should SQL parameters be handled?
faq.answer: Use parameterized query placeholders and pass values separately to reduce SQL injection risk.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide table names, column names, expected output shape, row limits, and any approved external API details.
